rationale:
Evidence from iteration 5 (score 938.5, best so far): oval, s-bend and slalom all finish 20/20, with progress about 0.996 to 0.998 and rms_error 0.004 to 0.007. The remaining score gap is in three places. (a) Line-loss events average 0.4 to 0.7 per run, and each event costs up to 15 points per unit progress (up to about 120 points in total). (b) Completion time is 2.2 to 2.7 s, which is worth at most 60 points. (c) Slalom has the highest steering_oscillation (0.30) and control_effort (6.7). Iteration 4 to 5 showed that reducing yaw inertia and mass helped a lot, while raising kd from 0.8 to 1.0 changed little. Controller gains and body geometry are therefore close to a local optimum, and the most promising untested lever is sensing coverage.

Change: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m. Larger footprints cover more of the 25 mm tape at each sensor position, so the sum of readings should fall below the 0.05 line-loss threshold less often on fast transitions or at the tape edge. Sensor positions (x = -0.03 to 0.03 at y = 0.06), weights, gains, base_speed, body, wheels, mass and line_loss are all unchanged, so the effect of this one change can be attributed. The trade-off is a coarser signal near the centre of the line, which could add a little steering jitter. Iteration 3 showed that widening the array hurt, but that changed spacing and reach, not footprint size, so it does not rule this out.

Expected result: line_loss_events falling from about 0.5 to under 0.2 on each track, with oval, s-bend and slalom completion staying at or near 100 percent. Score rising by roughly 20 to 50 points. If line losses do not fall, the cause is not footprint coverage, and the next test is either base_speed 1.0 for time or a small ki for drift on slalom.

Hypotheses to check: H1, line losses come from the tape leaving the sensor footprint at the array edges, so a larger footprint reduces them. H2, the remaining slalom oscillation comes from the signal over-responding at the tape edge. Measurements wanted: line_loss_events, completion_time and max_error per track, plus steering_oscillation and control_effort to see whether the coarser footprint adds jitter.
